author: Mark Atwood
text: API contract confidence: 85% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) the destroy: Option<&[Id]> finding (JMAP-1j9k.14) is borderline-opinion, labeled as such; reasonable people will disagree on whether the borrowed-slice vs owned-Vec divergence rises to engineering-meaningful. (b) The four CalendarEventGetParams findings (JMAP-1j9k.9/10/11) cluster around one struct — they are independent fixes but if the team decides to leave the struct as-is, all three become non-issues simultaneously. Uncertainty driven by: did not exhaustively cross-check every sibling extension-client (chat/contacts/tasks/sharing/filenode) to see if calendars-client is alone in these divergences or whether ALL extension-clients drifted from the canonical mail-client. If multiple siblings drifted in parallel, the propagation rule's 'change canonical first' guidance may already be silently in effect (canonical is the wrong reference). Did not check whether 'pub use' at the calendars-client crate root re-exports the same set of names as the canonical mail-client. Would raise confidence if: (1) a side-by-side audit confirms each sibling extension-client's /set, /query, /copy, *Params shapes and the canonical-template propagation rule was honored on previous changes; (2) a workspace-level decision is recorded somewhere (workspace AGENTS.md or a bd remember note) that records whether typed-create-maps or untyped-Value-creates are the canonical going forward.
